solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: British gang about to fail badly

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the British gang is read from right to left

parts.note: a mob is a gang or unruly crowd

explanation.surface: A British criminal gang is about to come badly unstuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of' but turns B + MOB around.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a show or film that bombs is a complete flop.

clue.text: Second group to go hiking

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a pack is a group, as of wolves or cub scouts

explanation.surface: A second group sets out on a hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal but is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to travel on foot carrying a rucksack is to go hiking.

clue.text: Guy on island, first character to display obsession

parts.note: a guy is a man
I is the map abbreviation for island
A is the first character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A man on an island is the first person to show an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a craze or fixation that grips someone is both.

clue.text: A joke one Master of Ceremonies pens is magnificent

indicators.note: pens means encloses, as a farmer pens sheep, so MC goes around the other letters

parts.note: a jest is a joke
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A compère writes a joke that turns out to be superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means 'encloses', as a sheep pen does.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight synonym: something grand and stately is described as both.

clue.text: Dutch city close to sea with ships on border

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of sea

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's fleet of ships
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A Dutch port near the sea with ships lining its border.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnhem, famous for a 1944 battle, is inland, so 'close to sea' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city in the Netherlands on the Rhine, capital of Gelderland.

clue.text: Former scheme a Conservative used to clarify

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a plan is a scheme
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An old plan a Tory politician used to make things clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: notes or remarks serving to make something clear are described this way.

clue.text: Spear I had thrown into river

indicators.note: thrown into says the I-had letters are put inside the river word

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls throwing a spear into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a three-pronged fishing spear, carried by Neptune.

clue.text: Warder, losing head, talked big

indicators.note: losing head means the warder word drops its first letter

parts.note: screw is British prison slang for a warder

explanation.surface: A prison guard who lost his temper had boasted loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of crow, which means to boast or brag; 'crowed' is the commoner form.

clue.text: Criticise prisoner, leader of malcontents, in study

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: in places the leading letter of malcontents inside the study word

parts.note: a den is a private room used as a study

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word malcontents

explanation.surface: A troublemaking inmate is criticised in the study by the ringleader.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to censure or denounce someone is to criticise them severely.

clue.text: New internet era for performer

indicators.note: New says the letters of internet era are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new internet age suits a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: anyone who amuses an audience, such as a singer or comedian.

clue.text: First class permit almost misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced says the remaining letters are put in the wrong order
almost means the word permit loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A first-class travel permit has nearly gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the T of PERMIT; 'misplaced' rearranges PERMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: top-quality or choice cuts of meat are called both.

clue.text: To be fair, carry on with tennis match?

definitions.meaning: to behave honourably and by the rules
literally to keep playing the match; the question mark flags the jokey literal reading

explanation.surface: Someone at a tennis match urges fair play and carrying on.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: acting honestly and sportingly is described with this phrase, which literally means to continue a contest.

clue.text: Very strong players getting support of press

indicators.note: in a down answer the players sit on top, held up by the press word beneath

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Actors gain the backing of the newspapers, which makes them very strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests newspapers but means IRON, which goes under CAST in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an alibi or guarantee that cannot be broken is called this, after the hard metal.

clue.text: In Civil Service, shock for people leading meetings

indicators.note: In places the shock word inside the Civil Service abbreviation

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: Something shocking happens in the Civil Service to the people running meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a jolt but means a thick mop on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A person presiding over a meeting is its chairman or chairwoman, shortened to this noun.

clue.text: In local ordered mainly hot drams, for example

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement
mainly means most of the word hot, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: In the pub, someone orders mostly hot toddies and drams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the T of HOT; 'ordered' shuffles LOCAL + HO. 'local' is British slang for a nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dram is a small measure of whisky, a strong drink.

clue.text: Phrase repeated in German translation

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words German translation, across their join

explanation.surface: A phrase is repeated in a German translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant or slogan said over and over, originally a sacred Hindu or Buddhist formula, is called this.

clue.text: Hardly anything for dessert

definitions.meaning: a British pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.surface: Next to nothing is left for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small trifling amount and the layered British pudding.

clue.text: Actor vainly playing a fortune teller

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of actor vainly are performing, rearranged

explanation.surface: A vain actor takes the part of a fortune teller.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone claiming to see the future, a seer or psychic, is described this way.

clue.text: Article: nothing about very small ear bone

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means the nothing word goes around the very letter

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: An item that has nothing to say about a tiny ear bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very small' looks like one phrase, but 'very' gives V and 'small' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: the incus, a tiny middle-ear bone, is named after the blacksmith's block it resembles.

clue.text: Ointment one gets from some herbal medicines

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ointment you get from certain herbal remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Ointment one gets' cannot stand in for the answer; 'one gets from' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a soothing salve or lotion applied to the skin.

clue.text: The girl tucking into a new pasty

indicators.note: tucking into says the girl word goes inside the a-plus-new letters

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl tucks into a new pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' is the pie in the surface but means pale, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pale, unhealthy-looking face is described as both.

clue.text: Insect on motorway bridge

parts.note: a fly is an insect
on and over both mean resting upon, as in a cover on or over a bed

explanation.surface: An insect lands on a motorway bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A road carried by a bridge over another road or a railway is called this.

clue.text: Early bird with egg initially laid in a month? Nonsense!

indicators.note: laid in says the bird and egg letters are set inside the month word

parts.note: May is a month of the year
the lark is a byword for rising early

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word egg

explanation.surface: A bird laying eggs early in a month is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags MAY as one example of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: humbug, claptrap or rubbish all mean foolish talk.

clue.text: Supporter eating large pastry dish

indicators.note: eating means the supporter word swallows the large abbreviation

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A fan tucks into a large pastry dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling, such as a quiche.
